m01:room.title: Guide-Star Metrology Rack
m01:room.job: Find how far the roll moved the star's image, and whether it still fits the slit.

m02:room.title: Photometric Standards Cell
m02:room.job: Find what share of the lamp's photons channel B really counts.

m03:room.title: Astrometry Plate Room
m03:room.job: Measure Earth's orbit, then turn a nearby star's yearly shift into a distance.

m04:room.title: Stellar Radiation Workroom
m04:room.job: Find a red star's surface heat from its colour, then its size from its power.

m05:room.title: Transit Photometry Bay
m05:room.job: Find the size of the body crossing our star, and the size of its orbit.

m06:room.title: The Echelle Reference Room
m06:room.job: Turn a star's tiny wobble into the mass of whatever is pulling it.

m07:room.title: The Foreground Rejection Lab
m07:room.job: Find how far away a moving speck is, and how fast it really goes.

m08:room.title: The Cluster Age Workroom
m08:room.job: Work out how long a heavy star can keep shining.

m09:room.title: The Extinction Correction Room
m09:room.job: Work out how much light the dust took, and put it back.

m10:room.title: The Transient Light-Curve Bay
m10:room.job: Find how far away a bright flash is, and how much power it gives off.

m11:room.title: X-ray Timing Cell
m11:room.job: Find how big a fast-flickering X-ray source can be, and what powers it.

m12:room.title: Rotation-Curve Room
m12:room.job: Weigh a galaxy from how fast its gas goes round.

m13:room.title: Redshift Standards Lab
m13:room.job: Measure how much a galaxy's light is stretched, and turn that into a distance.

m14:room.title: Foreground Separation Chamber
m14:room.job: Turn the receiver's volts into a sky temperature, and see how warm one patch is.

m15:room.title: Crew Safety Room
m15:room.job: Check two budgets for the observing window: the battery and the hot arm.
